findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "book_and_pay_transfer" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Book an airport transfer and pay for it now with a Stripe shared payment token (spt_...) the traveller approved, for example from their Link wallet. CHARGES the…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_transfer_quote, book_and_pay_transfer · Private data: get_transfer_quote, list_tours, start_tour_booking, get_booking_terms, book_and_pay_transfer · Public sink: find_transfer_destination, get_transfer_quote, start_transfer_booking, book_and_pay_transfer.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_transfer_quote, book_and_pay_transfer · Private data: get_transfer_quote, list_tours, start_tour_booking, get_booking_terms, book_and_pay_transfer · Public sink: find_transfer_destination, get_transfer_quote, start_transfer_booking, book_and_pay_transfer

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "list_tours" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
